pregunta: Me sale Permission denied (publickey) cuando hago git push, ¿qué debo revisar?
reference: No uses sudo ni privilegios elevados con Git, conéctate como el usuario git, verifica que tu clave SSH esté cargada con `ssh-add -l`, confirma la conexión con `ssh -vT git@github.com` y asegúrate de que la clave pública esté agregada a tu cuenta de GitHub.
respuesta:
El servidor rechaza tu clave SSH al hacer git push

1. No uses sudo con los comandos de Git; ejecuta git push sin privilegios elevados
2. Verifica que te conectas al servidor correcto con `ssh -vT git@`
3. Comprueba que tu clave está cargada en el agente SSH con `ssh-add -l`
4. Asegúrate de que la clave pública está añadida a tu cuenta de GitHub (o como deploy key si corresponde)

reference: GitHub elimina automáticamente las claves SSH inactivas, es decir, las que no se han usado en un año, como medida de seguridad. Puedes comprobarlo revisando el registro de seguridad de tu cuenta.
respuesta:
GitHub elimina automáticamente claves SSH inactivas para proteger la cuenta

1. Revisa el registro de seguridad de tu cuenta para confirmar que la clave no se usó durante más de un año
2. Si la clave estuvo inactiva, GitHub la habrá borrado automáticamente
3. Genera una nueva clave SSH y asóciala a tu cuenta de GitHub

# Deleted or missing SSH keys

GitHub automatically deletes inactive SSH keys to help keep accounts safe, such as after someone leaves a job or loses a computer.

You can check if you haven't used an SSH key in a year by reviewing your account's security log. For more information, see .

After your inactive SSH key is deleted, you must generate a new SSH key and associate it with your account. For more information, see  and .

# Error: We''re doing an SSH key audit

When using an unverified key to perform Git operations, you will be prompted to perform an audit of your SSH keys.

```shell
ERROR: We're doing an SSH key audit.
Reason: unverified due to lack of use
Please visit https://github.com/settings/ssh
to approve this key so we know it's safe.
Fingerprint: ab:08:46:83:ff:f6:c4:f8:a9:4e:68:6b:94:17:f2:46
fatal: could not read from remote repository
```

## Solving the issue

To fix this, you need to review your SSH keys and either reject or approve the unverified key. Clicking the URL link in the error message brings you to the SSH Settings page, where the unverified SSH key is highlighted in the SSH key list.

# Error: Host key verification failed

This error means that the server to which you're connecting presented a key that doesn't match the keys seen for this server in the past.

You may see this error if the server has changed its keys unexpectedly, in which case you should be able to find an official report from a trustworthy source announcing the change. If  changes its SSH host key, this will be announced on  at github.blog.

You can find an up-to-date list of 's public SSH keys on . You may need to add these keys to your `known_hosts` file. For more information, see .

# Error: Key already in use

## Finding where the key has been used

To determine where the key has already been used, open a terminal and type the `ssh` command. Use the `-i` flag to provide the path to the key you want to check:

```shell
$ ssh -T -ai ~/.ssh/id_rsa git@
# Connect to  using a specific ssh key
> Hi USERNAME! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not
> provide shell access.
```

The _username_ in the response is the account on  that the key is currently attached to. If the response looks something like "username/repo", the key has been attached to a repository as a _deploy key_.

To force SSH to use only the key provided on the command line, use `-o` to add the `IdentitiesOnly=yes` option:

```shell
ssh -v -o "IdentitiesOnly=yes" -i ~/.ssh/id_rsa git@
```

pregunta: El puerto 22 está bloqueado en mi red, ¿cómo me conecto a GitHub por SSH?
reference: Puedes probar SSH sobre el puerto HTTPS con `ssh -T -p 443 git@ssh.github.com`. Si funciona, clona el repositorio con `git clone ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/TU-USUARIO/TU-REPOSITORIO.git`. El nombre de host para el puerto 443 es ssh.github.com, no github.com, y los servidores proxy pueden interferir.
respuesta:
El puerto 22 está bloqueado, por lo que la conexión SSH directa a GitHub falla; se puede usar SSH sobre el puerto 443 (HTTPS).

1. Cambia la URL remota para usar el puerto 443, por ejemplo: `git clone ssh://git@ssh.github.com:443/TU-USUARIO/TU-REPOSITORIO.git`.
2. Edita tu archivo de configuración SSH (`~/.ssh/config`) y agrega:
3. ```text
4. Host ssh.github.com
5.     Hostname ssh.github.com
6.     Port 443
7.     User git
8. ```
9. Prueba la conexión con: `ssh -T -p 443 git@ssh.github.com`.
10. Si aparece el mensaje de advertencia sobre la huella del host, responde "yes" (ver fragmento 2).
11. Una vez autenticado, puedes usar los comandos habituales de Git (push, pull, etc.) con la URL configurada.

## Updating known hosts

The first time you interact with GitHub after switching to port 443, you may get a warning message
that the host wasn't found in `known_hosts`, or that it was found by another name.

```bash

    Port 443
    User git
```

pregunta: Me dice que la clave ya está en uso al agregar mi clave SSH, ¿qué significa?
reference: Significa que esa clave ya fue agregada a otra cuenta o repositorio. Para saber dónde se usa, ejecuta `ssh -T -ai ~/.ssh/id_rsa git@github.com`: el nombre de usuario de la respuesta es la cuenta a la que está asociada la clave, y si aparece algo como usuario/repo, está adjunta a un repositorio como deploy key. Para resolverlo, elimina la clave de la otra cuenta o repositorio y luego agrégala a tu cuenta.
respuesta:
El error “Key already in use” indica que la clave SSH que intentas agregar ya está asociada a otra cuenta o a un repositorio como deploy key

1. Ejecuta `ssh -T -ai ~/.ssh/id_rsa git@github.com` para ver a qué cuenta o repositorio está vinculada la clave
2. Si la clave está asociada a otro usuario o a un deploy key, elimínala de ese lugar (desde la configuración de SSH keys del otro usuario o del repositorio)
3. Si no puedes eliminarla, genera una nueva pareja de claves (`ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096 -C "tu_email"`) y agrega la nueva clave pública a tu cuenta
4. Una vez liberada, vuelve a agregar la clave con `ssh-add ~/.ssh/id_rsa` y verifica con `ssh -T git@github.com`

Puede pasar si el servidor cambió sus claves, y en ese caso debe existir un anuncio oficial (GitHub los publica en su blog). 3. Si no puedes confirmar la legitimidad del cambio, no te conectes y contacta al equipo de IT o al soporte del servidor

pregunta: ¿Cómo resuelvo un conflicto de merge desde la página del pull request en GitHub?
reference: Haz clic en el botón Resolve conflicts, localiza en el editor los marcadores de conflicto (<<<<<<<, ======= y >>>>>>>), edita el archivo para decidir qué cambios conservar y elimina los marcadores. Luego haz clic en Mark as resolved, repite el proceso con cada archivo en conflicto y finaliza con Commit merge.
respuesta:
El pull request tiene conflictos de merge y deben resolverse usando el editor web de GitHub

1. En la lista de Pull Requests, haz clic en el pull request que muestra el conflicto.
2. En la parte inferior del pull request, haz clic en **Resolve conflicts**.
3. En el editor que se abre, revisa cada marcador de conflicto; si hay varios, desplázate al siguiente y repite la resolución.
4. Una vez resueltos todos los conflictos, haz clic en **Mark as resolved**.
5. Si el botón **Resolve conflicts** está desactivado, resuelve el conflicto con otro cliente Git o la línea de comandos.

Hay un conflicto de merge en líneas idénticas y debe resolverse manualmente en la línea de comandos

1. Abre tu terminal o Git Bash.
2. Navega al repositorio con `cd REPOSITORY-NAME`.
3. Lista los archivos afectados por el conflicto (ver fragmento 1).
4. Edita cada archivo con conflicto, elige los cambios que deseas conservar y elimina los marcadores <<<<<<<, =======, >>>>>>>.
5. Una vez resueltos los archivos, realiza un commit de la resolución (ver fragmento 4).

# Resolving a merge conflict using the command line

Merge conflicts happen when competing changes are made to the same line of a file, or when one person edits a file and another person deletes the same file. See .

> [!TIP]
> You can use the conflict editor on  to resolve competing line change merge conflicts between branches that are part of a pull request. See .

## Competing line change merge conflicts

When competing changes affect the same lines, choose which changes to keep, then commit the resolution.

1. Open your terminal or Git Bash.
1. Navigate into the local Git repository that has the merge conflict.

   ```shell
   cd REPOSITORY-NAME
   ```

1. List the files affected by the merge conflict. In this example, the file _styleguide.md_ has a merge conflict.

1. If more than one file has a conflict, select the next file you want to edit on the left side of the page under "conflicting files" and repeat steps four through seven until you've resolved all merge conflicts in your pull request.
1. After you've resolved all your merge conflicts, click **Commit merge**. This merges the entire base branch into your head branch.

   !Screenshot of the editor to resolve a merge conflict in a pull request. The "Commit merge" button is outlined in dark orange.

1. If prompted, review the branch that you are committing to. You can update the head branch or, if available, create a new branch for the pull request. If the head branch is protected, you must create a new branch.

# Resolving a merge conflict on GitHub

You can resolve simple competing line change conflicts on . For other conflicts, use the command line. See .

If  is enabled for the repository, you can click **Fix with ** in the merge box to have  resolve conflicts automatically. See .

If a site administrator disables the merge conflict editor for pull requests between repositories, resolve merge conflicts on the command line.

> [!WARNING]
> Resolving conflicts on  merges the entire base branch into the head branch. If the head branch is the default or protected branch, you may be prompted to create a new head branch. See .

1. In the "Pull Requests" list, click the pull request with a merge conflict that you want to resolve.
1. Near the bottom of your pull request, click **Resolve conflicts**.

## Resolving merge conflicts

Resolving a merge conflict means choosing the final content that should appear after the branches are merged. The right tool depends on the type of conflict.

* Simple line conflicts can often be resolved on . See .
* More complex conflicts must be resolved in a local clone and pushed back to the pull request branch. See .
* If you have access to  and it is enabled for the repository,  can help resolve conflicts from the merge box. See .

On the command line, Git tells you when a merge cannot finish automatically. You cannot push the merged result until you resolve the conflict and commit the resolution.

pregunta: Una rama borró un archivo que otra rama editó, ¿cómo resuelvo ese conflicto?
reference: Decide si conservar o eliminar el archivo. Para conservarlo ejecuta `git add README.md` (con el nombre del archivo); para eliminarlo ejecuta `git rm README.md`. Después confirma el cambio con `git commit` y un mensaje.
respuesta:
Conflicto de merge donde una rama elimina un archivo y la otra lo modifica

1. Ejecuta `git status` para ver el archivo en conflicto (por ejemplo, aparecerá como `deleted by us:`).
2. Decide si deseas conservar el archivo editado o aceptar su eliminación:
3.   • Para conservar el archivo editado, restaura la versión del otro branch con `git checkout --theirs <archivo>` (o `git restore --source=MERGE_HEAD --staged <archivo>`), luego marca la resolución con `git add <archivo>`.
4.   • Para aceptar la eliminación, elimina el archivo del índice con `git rm <archivo>`.
5. Una vez marcado el archivo, finaliza el merge con `git commit` (el mensaje de commit ya incluirá la resolución).

# Resolving a merge conflict using the command line

Merge conflicts happen when competing changes are made to the same line of a file, or when one person edits a file and another person deletes the same file. See .

> [!TIP]
> You can use the conflict editor on  to resolve competing line change merge conflicts between branches that are part of a pull request. See .

## Competing line change merge conflicts

When competing changes affect the same lines, choose which changes to keep, then commit the resolution.

1. Open your terminal or Git Bash.
1. Navigate into the local Git repository that has the merge conflict.

   ```shell
   cd REPOSITORY-NAME
   ```

1. List the files affected by the merge conflict. In this example, the file _styleguide.md_ has a merge conflict.

## Resolving merge conflicts

Resolving a merge conflict means choosing the final content that should appear after the branches are merged. The right tool depends on the type of conflict.

* Simple line conflicts can often be resolved on . See .
* More complex conflicts must be resolved in a local clone and pushed back to the pull request branch. See .
* If you have access to  and it is enabled for the repository,  can help resolve conflicts from the merge box. See .

On the command line, Git tells you when a merge cannot finish automatically. You cannot push the merged result until you resolve the conflict and commit the resolution.

1. If more than one file has a conflict, select the next file you want to edit on the left side of the page under "conflicting files" and repeat steps four through seven until you've resolved all merge conflicts in your pull request.
1. After you've resolved all your merge conflicts, click **Commit merge**. This merges the entire base branch into your head branch.

   !Screenshot of the editor to resolve a merge conflict in a pull request. The "Commit merge" button is outlined in dark orange.

1. If prompted, review the branch that you are committing to. You can update the head branch or, if available, create a new branch for the pull request. If the head branch is protected, you must create a new branch.

# Creating a pull request

If you want to create a new branch for your pull request but don't have write permissions to the repository, you can fork the repository first. See  and .

When you create your pull request, you can specify which branch you want to merge your changes into. Pull requests can only be opened between two different branches.

## Creating the pull request

1. In the "Branch" menu, choose the branch that contains your commits.

   !Screenshot of the branch dropdown menu on the main page of a repository.

1. Use the _base_ branch dropdown menu to select the branch where you want to merge your changes. Then, use the _compare_ branch dropdown menu to choose the topic branch where you made your changes.

After your pull request has been reviewed, it can be merged into the repository. See .

To create a pull request, use the `gh pr create` subcommand.

```shell
gh pr create
```

To assign a pull request to an individual, use the `--assignee` or `-a` flags. You can use `@me` to self-assign the pull request.

```shell
gh pr create --assignee "@octocat"
```

To specify the branch into which you want the pull request merged, use the `--base` or `-B` flags. To specify the branch that contains commits for your pull request, use the `--head` or `-H` flags.

```shell
gh pr create --base my-base-branch --head my-changed-branch
```

To include a title and body for the new pull request, use the `--title` and `--body` flags.

# Pull request merges

Pull requests can be merged in different ways. The best strategy depends on how your team wants the repository history to look and how much detail you want to preserve from the pull request branch.

Choose this strategy when your team wants a linear history and the pull request commits are already organized clearly. If  cannot safely rebase the pull request automatically, you can rebase locally, resolve conflicts, and push the updated branch. See  and .

## Indirect merges

A pull request can be marked as merged if its head branch commits become reachable from the base branch outside that pull request. This can happen when the same commits are merged through another pull request or pushed directly to the default branch.

Indirect merges are uncommon, but they can affect automation and branch protection expectations. Pull requests merged indirectly are marked as `merged` even if branch protection rules on that pull request were not satisfied.
